slides.title: Preparation Decides the Value You Get
bullets: Preparation is the single biggest driver of congress value
The time window is short and KOL agendas fill weeks ahead
Improvising on the ground means arriving late to the best opportunities

slides.title: Map Your Objectives and Your People
bullets: Review the priority KOL and DOL list likely to attend
Decide who to see first and start coordinating meetings early
Speaker and leader agendas fill fast, so waiting costs you the meeting
Builds on the CRM and KOL mapping system kept updated year-round

slides.title: Immerse Yourself in the Scientific Program
bullets: Review the full program: plenaries, oral communications, posters
Study abstracts released weeks in advance where available
Anticipate what new data will be presented
Prepare informed questions instead of reacting on the spot

slides.title: Align the Internal Team First
bullets: Join the Medical Affairs pre-congress briefing
Ensure MSLs and stand or communications staff share one narrative
Same approved data, same approved language across the team
Prevents inconsistent messages that damage credibility

slides.title: Sort Logistics and Materials in Advance
bullets: Line up approved scientific materials: FAQs, backup literature, decks
Review congress-specific compliance rules on HCP interaction and hospitality
Plan movement between sessions in a schedule with constant overlap

slides.title: Preparation Is What the KOL Actually Feels
bullets: A well-prepared MSL uses limited time far more effectively
Every KOL senses the conversation was designed specifically for them
That feeling alone strengthens the scientific relationship

takeaway.title: What happens before the congress determines what you get out of it
bullets: Mapping people and content early beats improvising on site
Internal alignment protects the organization's scientific credibility
Logistics and materials prep frees up time for what actually matters
